Empirical p-values against a pooled permutation null

Source: R/inference.R
pooled_perm_pvalues.Rd

Computes one-sided empirical p-values for observed edge scores (larger = more extreme, e.g. \(|\hat\theta^{(1)}_{ij} - \hat\theta^{(2)}_{ij}|\)) against a null distribution pooled over all edges and permutations, and Benjamini-Hochberg adjusts them.

Usage

pooled_perm_pvalues(observed, null, tol = sqrt(.Machine$double.eps))

Arguments

observed

Numeric vector of observed scores, or a square matrix (the upper triangle is used, in upper.tri() order as in edge_index()).

null

Null scores: a numeric vector or matrix, or a list of them. All finite values are pooled. If observed is a matrix, list elements with the same dimensions contribute their upper triangle.

tol

Relative tolerance: a null value counts as at least as large as \(x\) if it is \(> x - tol \cdot \max(1, |x|)\), so that ties up to rounding error count as exceedances.

Value

A list with pvalue, \((1 + \#\{null \ge obs\}) / (1 + n_{null})\), and p_adj (BH-adjusted), one per observed edge. Missing observed scores give NA. If the pool has no finite values, all p-values are NA with a warning.

Details

Pooling gives a p-value resolution of about \(1 / (1 + B m)\) for \(B\) permutations and \(m\) edges, instead of \(1 / (1 + B)\) for per-edge nulls, which is fine enough to survive a BH correction over many edges. It assumes the per-edge null distributions are approximately exchangeable, which is reasonable for label-permutation nulls of comparable (e.g. standardized) scores.

See also

bayes_fdr()

Examples

set.seed(1)
p <- 6
null <- replicate(50, abs(matrix(rnorm(p * p), p)), simplify = FALSE)
obs <- abs(matrix(rnorm(p * p), p)); obs[1, 2] <- 4
pp <- pooled_perm_pvalues(obs, null)
cbind(edge_index(p), pvalue = pp$pvalue, p_adj = pp$p_adj)[1:3, ]
#>   i j node1 node2      pvalue      p_adj
#> 1 1 2    V1    V2 0.001331558 0.01997337
#> 2 1 3    V1    V3 0.924101198 0.96404794
#> 3 2 3    V2    V3 0.382157124 0.84458817
